key_insight: Charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into CO is strongly metal-dependent, with electron injection dominating because the CO LUMO lies closer to the metal Fermi level than the HOMO.
engineering_relevance: These results guide the choice of nanoparticle material for photocatalytic interfaces by identifying metals that maximize direct hot-carrier transfer rather than wasteful thermalization.
method: Combined ab initio DFT for adsorbate–metal electronic structure with macroscopic electrodynamics for localized surface plasmons.
Predicted hot-electron and hot-hole injection rates from large spherical nanoparticles into adsorbed CO.
Compared nine metals spanning plasmonic and non-plasmonic classes: Ag, Au, Cu, Al, Ni, Rh, Pd, Ir, Pt.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computed injection-rate comparisons across nine metals, finding the largest optical-range electron injection for Al, Ag, Cu, and Au, with Cu and Au additionally showing strong plasmonic enhancement.
watch_item: The model is specific to large spherical nanoparticles and CO adsorption, so trends may change for different particle shapes, sizes, or adsorbates.
paper_title: Material dependence of direct light-induced charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbates
